item.case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
item.title: Voyager One Against the References

turns.text: Make a silent 9-second widescreen fact clip about Voyager 1, using NASA's mission page as the reference: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . Three equal-length scenes: 'Launched: September 5, 1977', 'Jupiter flyby: 1979', 'Saturn flyby: 1980'. Keep 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible. Show the probe near Earth, Jupiter, then Saturn; match its real dish-and-boom design. Don't mix in Voyager 2's Uranus or Neptune visits.

item.tests: Tests whether a factual film matches a named reference in dates, mission identity, spacecraft appearance and scene order.

answer_sheet.Facts to include: Voyager 1 launched September 5, 1977, flew by Jupiter in 1979 and flew by Saturn in 1980.
answer_sheet.Length and scene order: 9 seconds total: three 3-second scenes showing Earth, Jupiter and Saturn in that order.
answer_sheet.Wording: Use exactly the five supplied labels. Keep Voyager 1 and Source: NASA Science visible throughout.
answer_sheet.Sound: Completely silent, with no narration, music or sound effects.
answer_sheet.Visual style: Your call, provided the spacecraft matches the real dish-and-boom design and the planets are recognizable.

must_haves: Three scenes appear in order, each lasting approximately three seconds: probe near Earth, near Jupiter, then near Saturn.
Each scene displays its corresponding date caption exactly, with 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible throughout.
The probe consistently has Voyager's large circular communications dish and projecting instrument booms, not solar-panel wings or a generic satellite body.
Jupiter is visibly banded and Saturn has prominent rings; neither is replaced with Uranus or Neptune.
The output contains no Uranus or Neptune flyby claims and no conflicting dates.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: Create a completely silent, widescreen educational fact clip about VOYAGER 1, exactly 9 seconds total. No audio track, narration, music, sound effects or speech. Reference attribution: NASA Science Voyager 1 mission page https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . Use these accurate supplied facts: Voyager 1 launched September 5, 1977, flew by Jupiter in 1979 and Saturn in 1980. NOT Voyager 2. Never depict Uranus or Neptune. Three equal scenes with hard cuts precisely at 3.0 and 6.0 seconds. Scene 1 (0.0–3.0s): Voyager 1 in space near recognizable blue Earth with white clouds; exact scene label 'Launched: September 5, 1977'. Scene 2 (3.0–6.0s): same probe near recognizable Jupiter with cream and orange cloud bands and Great Red Spot; exact scene label 'Jupiter flyby: 1979'. Scene 3 (6.0–9.0s): same probe near recognizable pale-gold Saturn with its prominent broad thin rings; exact scene label 'Saturn flyby: 1980'. Only the current scene label appears during its assigned three seconds. Throughout every frame from start through finish keep the exact title 'Voyager 1' visibly fixed at upper left and the exact credit 'Source: NASA Science' visibly fixed at lower right. These five supplied labels are the ONLY text anywhere. Crisp, large readable white sans-serif typography on subtle dark backing with safe margins; scene labels fixed at bottom left clear of credit. Scientific documentary-style 3D illustration, restrained slow camera drift within each scene, coherent realistic probe design throughout: large white parabolic high-gain antenna dish attached to compact metallic instrument bus, long slender magnetometer boom, science instrument boom, RTG boom and thin antenna rods, gold insulation details. Not a generic winged satellite: no solar panels. Keep spacecraft fully framed and planets recognizable. Illustrative mission montage, not actual archival footage. No extra labels, logos, captions, numbers or invented dates. Maintain all exact spelling and punctuation.
